utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Officer, please make sure that his channel is -- he's got the right channel on? Yeah. Okay. So, Madam Registrar, good afternoon to you. Could you call the case, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honour. This is case number IT-01-45-I, the Prosecutor versus Ante Gotovina.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thank you, Madam. Mr. Gotovina, good afternoon to you. I want to make sure that you are able to follow the proceedings in our own language, in other words that you are receiving interpretation. You have to say yes or no.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you. You can remain seated for the time being. If at any time you're not receiving interpretation in a language that you can understand, or if the reception of the interpretation is not satisfactory, either because the sound level is not correct or for any other reason, please draw my attention straight away. It's very important that throughout the entire sitting you are able to follow the proceedings at any given moment. Appearances. Could I have the appearances for the Prosecution, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honour. On behalf of the Prosecution, my name is Alex Whiting. I'm joined today on my left by Ms. Laurie Sartorio, Ms. Katherine Gallagher, behind me Ms. Haike Bock, and our case manager, Ms. Lakshmie Walpita.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thank you, Mr. Whiting, and good afternoon to you and your team. I know because I have been informed because Registrar has appointed duty counsel to look after the interests of the accused for today's Initial Appearance. Mr. Knoops, could you identify yourself, please, and confirm what I have just stated.

utterances.speaker: MR. KNOOPS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. Good afternoon. My name is Geert Alexander Knoops. I am indeed appearing as duty counsel for the accused.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thank you, and good afternoon to you, Mr. Knoops, and I thank you so much on behalf of the Tribunal for having accepted this onus for today. Now, Mr. Gotovina, before I proceed any further it is my duty here to explain to you that you have a fundamental right here to remain silent throughout the entire proceedings. In other words, no one can force you to answer any question that may be put to you as we proceed. And before we come to the most important part of the Initial Appearance, I have decided that I will give some details -- explain some of the details of the indictment and about the indictment itself. The accused, Ante Gotovina, was included in the indictment with case number IT-01-45, which was signed on the 22nd of May, 2001, filed on the 31st of May of that year, and which was kept under seal. That indictment was confirmed by my colleague, Judge Fuad Riad on the 8th of June, 2001, and kept under seal. An amended indictment was also kept under seal, was filed by the OTP, by the Office of the Prosecutor, on the 19th of February of last year, 2004, and that indictment, that amended indictment, was confirmed by my colleague Judge Kevin Parker of the -- on the 24th of February of that year. On the 8th of March, 2004, Judge Parker issued an order making public the amended indictment that he had confirmed. The accused, as everyone knows now, was arrested in Tenerife, Spain, on Wednesday, the 7th of December, 2005, and last Saturday, that's the 10th of December, he was transferred to The Hague that is the seat of this Tribunal. Before I proceed any further, let me give you some information on the details of the indictment against you, Mr. Gotovina. This will help you understand the nature of the charges that the Prosecutor has brought against you in virtue of the indictment that will be read out to you later on, and also my explanation will help members of the public following these proceedings to understand what these proceedings are all about and what you are being charged with. The amended indictment alleges that you, Mr. Gotovina, was born -- you were born on the 12th of October, 1955, on the island of Pasman within the municipality of Zadar in the Republic of Croatia, which then formed part of the Socialist Federal Republic of Yugoslavia. According to the Prosecutor, at all times relevant to the indictment, you were the commander of the Split Operative Zone of the Croatian army, Hrvatska Vojska. It is also alleged in the indictment that you were also the overall operational commander of the Croatian forces that were deployed as part of Operations Storm in the southern portion of the Krajina region. According to the indictment, the so-called Operation Storm was a military offensive launched by the Republic of Croatia on the 4th of August, 1995, with the specific objective of re-taking the Krajina region, including the municipalities, in whole or in part, of Benkovac, Gracac, Knin, Obrovac, Sibenik, Sinj, and Zadar. While the Croatian government announced Operation Storm had been successfully completed by the 7th of August, 1995, it is indeed being alleged that follow-up actions continued until about the 15th of November of 1995. The amended indictment alleges that during and after Operation Storm, Croatian forces attacked and took control of towns, villages, and hamlets in the southern portion of the Krajina region, during which they subjected the local Serb population to persecutions and plundered and destroyed the property in the municipalities in Benkovac, Donji Labac, Drnis, Gospic, Gracac, Knin, Korenica, Obrovac, Sibenik, Sinj, and Zadar, thereby forcing the Krajina Serbs to flee. The amended indictment further alleges that Croatian forces killed at least 150 Serbs in Krajina while subjecting large numbers of others to inhumane treatment, humiliation, and degradation. Mr. Gotovina, you are charged with four counts of crime against humanity under Article 5 of the Statute of this Tribunal and with three counts of the violations of laws or customs of war under Article 3 of the Statute of this Tribunal. The amended indictment alleges, also, that a joint criminal enterprise, of which you formed part, together with others, including Ivan Cermak and Mladen Markac, who you know are already here, and also the late president of Croatia, Franjo Tudjman existed, and the purpose of this joint criminal enterprise was the forcible and permanent removal of the Serb population from the Krajina region, including by plundering, damaging, or destroying the property of the Serb population, so as to discourage or prevent members of that population from returning to their homes. You are further charged, in terms of the amended indictment, with individual criminal responsibility pursuant to Article 7(1) of our Statute, and that is for having acting individually or in concert with others, planned, instigated, ordered, committed, or otherwise aided and abetted in the planning, preparation, or execution of the crimes charged in the amended indictment or that you foresaw the likelihood that they would be committed. Then you are also charged under Article 7(3) of our Statute with superior command responsibility. The Prosecution is alleging that you knew or had reason to know that all crimes alleged in the amended indictment were about to be committed or had been committed by your subordinates and that indeed you failed to take the necessary and reasonable measures to protect -- to prevent such acts or to punish the perpetrators thereof. The Prosecution alleges in the amended indictment that all the crimes mentioned therein occurred between the 4th of August, 1995, and the 15th of November of that year in the southern portion of the Krajina region and were directed against the Serb population in the territory of the Krajina region. The Vice-President of this Tribunal, Judge Parker, acting as President, by order dated the 9th of December, 2005, assigned this case, your case, to my Trial Chamber, that is Trial Chamber II. I am the President of Trial Chamber II, and in an order which I signed this morning, I designated myself as Pre-Trial Judge for the purpose of the Initial Appearance of the accused. I will now proceed to the more substantive part of the Initial Appearance in accordance or as required by our Rules, and the relative rule is Rule 62. And once I have gone through these preliminaries, then I will move to the most important formality of this Initial Appearance, and that is formally charge you and ask you whether you wish to enter a plea to the charges brought against you today or later and what kind of plea you wish to enter in any case. Now, Mr. Gotovina, could you please stand up.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Now, my first responsibility relates to presentation. I -- you may have noted -- you would have noted, for sure, that earlier on I mentioned that I was noticing the presence in the courtroom of Mr. Knoops, who I understood had been appointed as duty counsel by the Registrar for the purpose of representing you for today's Initial Appearance only. You are aware of that, Mr. Gotovina, aren't you?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I am.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thank you. And would you like to say anything in relation to your being represented this afternoon by Mr. Knoops?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I have nothing to say.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thank you. Rule 62 requires of me to put to you a series of questions before -- then I charge you formally and ask you if you wish to enter a plea. Could you please give me your full name for the record.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Ante Gotovina.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Do you have any nicknames by which you are referred to?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Could you give me your date of birth, please.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The 12th of October, 1955.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thank you. And your place of birth, please.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Zadar.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I am going to ask you now the address at which you resided, your last address, which you resided before you arrived here. I'm giving you the option to tell me that, if you wish so, in open session, public session, or in private session. Private session would mean that only the persons inside these four walls here, and therefore excluding the members of the public, would hear what you have to say. What's your choice?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Tenerife, the Canary Islands, in Spain.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Do you have a specific address that you could give me?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No. No, Your Honour, I don't.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, I want to make sure that the members of your family have been informed about your transfer to The Hague and also your state of detention in the UN Detention Unit here in The Hague. Can you confirm that to me, please?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Have you had an opportunity to contact the members of your family?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I also want to make sure that your embassy, the embassy of the Republic of Croatia, has been informed of your presence and detention here in The Hague. I would take it that the embassy has been informed, but are you aware as to whether the embassy has been informed or not?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, they have been informed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you. Do you require me to do anything on your behalf as regards contacting your family or any member from the embassy of the Republic of Croatia?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Gotovina, please do sit down.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: The purpose of your arraignment here today is not only to formally charge you and ask you to enter a plea, but a publicly inform you of certain rights, very important rights, that you enjoy, both under international law but also in terms of our Statute and our Rules. Indeed I am going to ask the registrar to read out to you the relevant passages from the Statute of this Tribunal, particularly Articles 20 and 21 of our Statute. And then I will add a few words of my own and proceed to make sure that you have understood or that you understood fully the nature and the importance of these rights that you enjoy now and also later, throughout the continuance of all these proceedings against you. Madam Registrar, could you kindly read out slowly and in English Article 20 of the Statute of the Tribunal? After which you can then proceed to read Article 21. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. Article 20: "Commencement and conduct of trial proceedings. "1. The Trial Chambers shall ensure that a trial is fair and expeditious and that proceedings are conducted in accordance with the Rules of Procedure and Evidence with full respect for the rights of the accused and due regard for the protection of victims and witnesses. "2. A person against whom an indictment has been confirmed shall, pursuant to an order or an arrest warrant of the International Tribunal, be taken into custody, immediately informed of the charges against him, and transferred to the International Tribunal. "3. The Trial Chamber shall read the indictment, satisfy itself that the rights of the accused are respected, confirm that the accused understands the indictment, and instructs the accused to enter a plea. The Trial Chamber shall then set the date for trial. "4. The hearings shall be public unless the Trial Chamber decides to close the proceedings in accordance with its Rules of Procedure and Evidence." Article 21: "Rights of the accused. "1. All persons shall be equal before the International Tribunal. "2. In the determination of charges against him, the accused shall be entitled to a fair and public hearing, subject to Article 22 of the Statute. "3. The accused shall be presumed innocent until proved guilty, according to the provisions of the present Statute. "4. In the determination of any charge against the accused, pursuant to the present Statute, the accused shall be entitled to the following minimum guarantees and full equality: (a) to be informed promptly and in detail in a language which he understands of the nature and cause of the charge against him; (b) to have adequate time and facilities for the preparation of his defence and to communicate with counsel of his own choosing; (c) to be tried without undue delay; (d) to be tried in his presence and to defend himself in person or through legal assistance of his own choosing; to be informed, if he does not have legal assistance, of this right; and to have legal assistance assigned to him in any case where the interests of justice so require and without payment by him in any such case if he does not have sufficient means to pay for it; (e) to examine, have examined the witnesses against him and to obtain the attendance and examination of witnesses on his behalf under the same conditions as witnesses against him; (f) to have the free assistance of an interpreter if he cannot understand or speak the language used in the Tribunal; (g) not to be compelled to testify against himself or to confess guilt."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thank you so much, Madam. Mr. Gotovina, do you understand the importance of these rights which Madam Registrar has just read out to you?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I have.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Do you wish me to explain any of these rights before we continue?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I feel there's no need for that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. I will tell you -- you may sit down. I will tell you a couple of things, namely that in this Tribunal every accused is entitled to self-representation, in other words every accused can opt to defend himself or herself. That's number one. Alternatively, an accused can also ask to be represented by counsel of his own choosing. That right is not absolute. In other words, you cannot bring forward any person you like, however qualified that person may be in your own mind, to represent you. We have our own rules and standards by which we operate, and that person, before being able to represent you, must first be approved by the registrar. We also have in place a system of legal aid, which may or may not be applicable to you in this case. That depends on an assessment that the registrar makes after consultations with you and maybe investigations, too. We only intervene if you disagree with the assessment of the registrar and only if we come to the conclusion that the registrar has exercised his discretion unreasonably and in a manifest -- and manifestly so. You also have the right under Rule 65 of our Tribunal to ask to be released provisionally under bail. I am sure that you will be advised on this, whether it's the case of filing such a request or not by the counsel that will be assisting you. Last but not least is that later on you will be appearing before the Trial Chamber regularly until we come to trial, and I'll explain the procedure very shortly. And each time you appear, you enjoy the right that I mentioned to you in the very beginning, namely that you have a right to remain silent and that you cannot at any moment be compelled to state anything or to testify against yourself or to confess any guilt. Mr. Gotovina, have you been served with a copy of the amended indictment in your own language?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Have you read it?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have, and I have understood it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. I thank you. That spares me having to put the next question. Now, our Rules require me to read out the amended indictment to you. I know, because I have been informed already, that you were prepared to waive this right and take the amended indictment as read. However, I think that given that you have been a fugitive for the past four years and that for most of the time this indictment was kept under seal, I think I owe it to everyone that the indictment is read out in full. So please, make yourself comfortable, and Madam Registrar would kindly read out the entire indictment in full. When we come to the appendices, let -- I'll tell you what's going to happen. Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. "The Prosecutor of the International Criminal Tribunal for the former Yugoslavia, pursuant to her authority under Article 18 of the Statute of the International Criminal Tribunal for the former Yugoslavia charges: "Ante Gotovina with crime against humanity and violation of the laws or customs of war, as set forth below: "The accused, Ante Gotovina, was born on 12th October, 1955, on the island of Pasman within the municipality of Zadar in the Republic of Croatia, then part of the Socialist Federal Republic of Yugoslavia. "Ante Gotovina, a former French Legionnaire of the rank of chief corporal, returned to Croatia in June 1991, whereupon he was appointed chief of the operations and training of the 1st Brigade of the Zbor Narodne Garde, (National Guard Corps). From February to April 1992, he was deputy to the commander of the special unit of the Main Staff of the Croatian army, the Hrvatska Vojska (the "HV"), and from April to October 1992, he was assigned to the Croatian Defence Council, Hrvatsko Vijece Obrane (the "HVO"). "On 9 October 1992, Ante Gotovina, holding the rank of brigadier, was appointed the commander of the Split operative zone of the HV (which in 1993 was re-named the Split Military District), and held that command until March 1996. On the 30th of May, 1994, he was promoted to the rank of major general. By early August 1995, he had been promoted to the rank of Colonel General. "On the 4th of August, 1995, the Republic of Croatia launched a military offensive known as "Oluja" or "Storm" ("Operation Storm"), with the objective of re-taking the Krajina region. Ante Gotovina was the overall operational commander of the Croatian forces that were deployed as part of Operation Storm in the southern portion of the Krajina region, including the municipalities in whole or in part of Benkovac, Gracac, Knin, Obrovac, Sibenik, Sinj, and Zadar. On the 7th of August, 1995, the Croatian government announced that the operation had been successfully completed. Follow-up actions continued until about the 15th of November, 1995. In early August 1995, following the re-taking of the Krajina region, Ante Gotovina moved his headquarters to Knin, the capital of the Krajina region, which was located within the Split Military District. "On the 12th of March, 1996, the President of the Republic of Croatia, Franjo Tudjman ("President Tudjman"), appointed Ante Gotovina Chief of the HV Inspectorate. "Individual and superior criminal responsibility. "Ante Gotovina is individually criminally responsible for the crimes which are referred to in Articles 3 and 5 of the Statute of the Tribunal and which are alleged in this Amended Indictment pursuant to Article 7(1) of the Statute of the Tribunal. Acting individually or in concert with others, the accused planned, instigated, ordered, committed, or otherwise aided and abetted in the planning, preparation, or execution of such crimes, or foresaw the likelihood that they would be committed. "By using the word 'committed' in the Amended Indictment, the Prosecutor also includes acts that the accused committed by participating in a joint criminal enterprise. During and after Operation Storm, at all times relevant to this Amended Indictment, Ante Gotovina, with others, including Ivan Cermak, Mladen Markac, and President Franjo Tudjman, participated in a criminal joint enterprise, the common purpose of which was the forcible and permanent removal of the Serb population from the Krajina region, including by plunder, damage, or outright destruction of the property of the Serb population, so as to discourage or prevent members of that population from returning to their homes and resuming habitation. "The crimes enumerated in Counts 1 and 3 to 6 of this Amended Indictment were within the common purpose of the joint criminal enterprise. The accused had the state of mind necessary for the commission of these crimes. "The crimes enumerated in Counts 2 and 7 and, as an alternative to the allegations in paragraph 8, Counts 1 and 3 to 6, were the natural and foreseeable consequences of the execution of the joint criminal enterprise and the accused was so aware. "During Operation Storm and its aftermath, Croatian forces attacked and took control of towns, villages, and hamlets in the southern portion of the Krajina region. Pursuant to the orders of Ante Gotovina, these forces carried out the acts which give rise to Counts 1 and 3 to 6. By his acts and omissions, the accused thereby encouraged others, including Croatian civilians, to also perpetrate those acts that give rise to those charges. Further, the accused, Ante Gotovina, had a duty to restore and ensure public order and safety, and he failed to fulfil this duty. "As the overall operational commander, Ante Gotovina exercised de jure and/or de facto command and control over Croatian forces during Operation Storm. In the aftermath of Operation Storm, Ante Gotovina retained command and control of HV forces that continued to be deployed in the southern portion of Krajina region. "Ante Gotovina, while holding a position of superior authority, is also individually criminally responsible for the acts or omissions of his subordinates, pursuant to Article 7(3) of the Statute of the Tribunal. A superior is responsible for the criminal acts of his subordinates if he knew or had reason to know that his subordinates were about to commit such acts or had done so, and the superior failed to take the necessary reasonable measures to prevent such acts or to punish the subordinates. "Ante Gotovina had the power, authority, and responsibility to prevent or punish serious violations of international humanitarian law committed by Croatian forces during and after Operation Storm. The accused knew, or had reason to know, that all crimes alleged within this Amended Indictment were about to be committed or had been committed by his subordinates, and he failed to take necessary and reasonable measures to prevent acts or to punish the perpetrators thereof. The accused is therefore individually criminally responsible under Article 7(3) of the Statute of the Tribunal. "General allegations: "At all times relevant to this Amended Indictment, a state of armed conflict existed in the Krajina region of the Republic of Croatia in the territory of the former Yugoslavia. "At all times relevant to this Amended Indictment, the accused, Ante Gotovina, was required to abide by the laws and customs governing the conduct of war, including Common Article 3 of the Geneva Conventions of 1949. "The acts or omissions alleged against the accused in this Amended Indictment, which constitute crimes against humanity, are crimes punishable by Article 5 of the Statute of the Tribunal, and were part of a widespread or systematic attack directed against a civilian population, namely the Serb population of the southern portion of the Krajina region. "In this Amended Indictment, every reference to 'Croatian forces' means and includes those units of the HV, the Croatian Air Force or the HRZ, and units of the RH MUP that participated in Operation Storm and/or its aftermath, and also the civilian and Special Police in the southern part of the Krajina region. "The Count in the Amended Indictment in relation to murder and the Count of persecution insofar as it relies on the acts of murder, allege the totality of these acts. The Schedule to these Counts set forth only a small number of individual incidents for the purpose of specificity of pleading. "The general allegations contained in the previous paragraphs are re-alleged and incorporated into each of the relevant charges set out below. "Count 1: Persecutions. "Between 4th of August, 1995, and the 15th of November, 1995, the accused, Ante Gotovina, acting individually and/or in concert with other members of the joint criminal enterprise, planned, instigated, ordered, committed, or otherwise aided and abetted in the planning, preparations, or execution of persecutions of the Krajina Serb population in the southern part of the Krajina region. "The crimes of persecutions was perpetrated throughout the following -- through the following: "Plunder of public or private property. "Between the 4th of August, 1995, and the 15th of November, 1995, Croatian forces systematically plundered the property of the Krajina Serbs, including their homes, outbuildings, barns, and livestock in the towns, villages, and the hamlets of the municipalities of Benkovac, Donji Lapac, Drnis, Gospic, Gracac, Knin, Korenica, Obrovac, Sibenik, Sinj, and Zadar. "Destruction of property. "Between the 4th of August, 1995, and the 15th of November, 1995, Croatian forces systematically set fire to or otherwise destroyed villages, homes, outbuildings and barns belongings to the Krajina Serbs, killed their livestock and spoiled their wells. Thousands of dwellings in the municipalities of Benkovac, Donji Lapac, Drnis, Gospic, Gracac, Knin, Korenica, Obrovac, Sibenik, Sinj, and Zadar were damaged or destroyed. "Deportation/forced displacement. "Between the 4th of August, 1995, and the 15th of November, 1995, Croatian forces directed violent and intimidating acts against Krajina Serbs, including the plunder and destruction of their property, thereby forcing them to flee the southern portion of the Krajina region. "These acts were intended to discourage or prevent those who had already fled the area, either immediately before or during Operation Storm in anticipation of an armed conflict, from returning to their homes. The effect of these violent and intimidating acts was a deportation and/or displacement of tens of thousands of Krajina Serbs to Bosnia and Herzegovina and Serbia. "The Prosecution alleges that the following two acts were natural and foreseeable consequences of the joint criminal enterprise, and on that basis also contributed to the offence of persecutions. "Murder. "Before the 4th of August, 1995, and the 15th of November, 1995, Croatian forces murdered at least 150 Krajina Serbs. Specifically referred to in this Amended Indictment are the murders of one person in the Benkovac municipality, 30 persons in the Knin municipality, and one person in the Korenica municipality. "Other inhumane acts. "Between the 4th of August, 1995, and the 15th of November, 1995, large numbers of Krajina Serbs were subjected to inhumane treatment, humiliation, and degradation by Croatian forces beating and assaulting them. "Alternatively, the accused, Ante Gotovina, knew or had reason to know that forces under his effective control were committing the acts described in paragraphs 21 through 26 above, or had done so, including as a result of having been so informed by representatives of the international community. The accused, Ante Gotovina, failed to take necessary and reasonable measures to prevent the commission of such acts or punish the perpetrators thereof. "By these acts and omissions, the accused, Ante Gotovina, did commit: "Count 1: A crime against humanity, namely persecutions on political, racial, and religious grounds, punishable under Article 5(h) read with Articles 7(1) and 7(3) of the Statute of the Tribunal. "Count 2: Murder. "Between the 4th of August, 1995, and the 15th of November, 1995, Croatian forces murdered at least 150 Krajina Serbs by meaning -- by means of shooting, burning, or stabbing. Specifically referred to in this Amended Indictment are the murders of one person in the Benkovac municipality, 30 persons in the Knin municipality, and one person in the Korenica municipality. "Listed in the schedule, attached hereto, are further particulars of such murders. "Between the 4th of August, 1995, and the 15th of November, 1995, the accused, Ante Gotovina, knew or had reason to know that forces under his effective control were about to murder Krajina Serbs, as described in paragraph 28 above, or had done so. The accused, Ante Gotovina, failed to take necessary and reasonable measures to prevent the commission of such acts or punish the perpetrators thereof. "By these acts and omissions, the accused, Ante Gotovina, did commit: "Count 2: A violation of the laws or customs of war, namely murder, as recognised by Common Article 3(1)(a) of the Geneva Conventions of 1949, punishable under Article 3 read with Article 7(3) of the Statute of the Tribunal. "Count 3: Plunder of property. "Between the 4th of August and the 15th of November, 1995, Croatian forces systematically plundered the property of the Krajina Serbs, including their homes, outbuildings, barns, and livestock in the towns, villages, and hamlets of the municipalities of Benkovac, Donji Lapac, Drnis, Gospic, Gracac, Knin, Korenica, Obrovac, Sibenik, Sinj, and Zadar. "The accused, Ante Gotovina, acting individually and/or in concert with other members of the joint criminal enterprise, planned, instigated, ordered, committed, or otherwise aided and abetted in the planning, preparation, or execution of the acts of plunder of property. "Alternatively, the accused, Ante Gotovina, knew, or had reason to know, that forces under his effective control were about to commit the acts described in paragraphs 30 above or had done so. The accused, Ante Gotovina, failed to take necessary and reasonable measures to prevent the commission of such acts or punish the perpetrators thereof. "By these acts or omissions, the accused, Ante Gotovina, did commit: "Count 3: A violation of the laws or customs of war, namely plunder of public or private property, punishable under Article 3(e) read with Articles 7(1) and 7(3) of the Statute of the Tribunal. "Count 4: Wanton destruction of cities, towns, or villages. "Between the 4th of August, 1995, and the 15th of November, 1995, Croatian forces systematically set fire to or otherwise destroyed villages, homes, outbuildings, and barns belonging to Krajina Serbs, killed their livestock, and spoiled their wells. Thousands of dwellings in the municipalities of Benkovac, Donji Lapac, Drnis, Gospic, Gracac, Knin, Korenica, Obrovac, Sibenik, Sinj, and Zadar were destroyed. "The accused, Ante Gotovina, acting individually and/or in concert with other members of the joint criminal enterprise, planned, instigated, ordered, committed, or otherwise aided and abetted in the planning, preparation, or execution of the acts of destruction of property. "Alternatively, the accused, Ante Gotovina, knew or had reason to know that forces under his effective control or subordinate to him were about to commit the acts described in paragraph 33 above or had done so. The accused, Ante Gotovina, failed to take necessary and reasonable measures to prevent the commission of such acts or punish the perpetrators thereof. "By these acts and omissions, the accused, Ante Gotovina, did commit: "Count 4: A violation of the laws or customs of war, namely wanton destruction of cities, towns, or villages, punishable under Article 3(b) read with Articles 7(1) and 7(3) of the Statute of the Tribunal. "Counts 5 and 6: Deportation and forced displacement. "Between the 4th of August, 1995, and 15th of November, 1995, Croatian forces directed violent and intimidating acts against Krajina Serbs, including the plunder and destruction of their property, thereby forcing them to flee the southern portion of the Krajina region. "These acts were intended to discourage or prevent those who had already fled the area, either immediately, before, or during Operation Storm in anticipation of an armed conflict, from returning to their homes. The effect of these violent and intimidating acts was the deportation and/or displacement of tens of thousands of Krajina Serbs to Bosnia and Herzegovina and Serbia. "The accused, Ante Gotovina, acting individually and/or in concert with others, including Ivan Cermak, Mladen Markac, and President Franjo Tudjman, planned, instigated, ordered, committed, or otherwise aided and abetted in the planning, preparation, or execution of the deportation and forced displacement of the Krajina Serb population. "Alternatively, the accused, Ante Gotovina, knew or had reason to know that forces under his effective control were about to commit the acts described in paragraph 36 and 37 above, or had done so. The accused, Ante Gotovina, failed to take necessary and reasonable measures to prevent the commission of such acts or punish the perpetrators thereof. "By these acts and omissions, the accused, Ante Gotovina, did commit: "Count 5: A crime against humanity, namely deportation, published -- punishable under Article 5(d) read with Articles 7(1) and 7(3) of the Statute of the Tribunal. "Count 6: A crime against humanity, namely other inhumane acts (forced displacement), punishable under Article 5(i) read with Articles 7(1) and 7(3) of the Statute of the Tribunal. "Count 7: Other inhumane acts. "Between the 4th of August, 1995, and the 15th of November, 1995, Croatian forces subjected many of the Krajina Serbs to inhumane treatment, humiliation, and degradation, by beating and assaulting them. "Between the 4th of August, 1995, and the 15th of November, 1995, the accused, Ante Gotovina, knew or had reason to know that forces under his effective control were about to commit the acts described in paragraph 40 above, or had done so. The accused, Ante Gotovina, failed to take necessary and reasonable measures to prevent the commission of such acts or punish the perpetrators thereof. "By these acts and omissions, the accused, Ante Gotovina, did commit: "Count 7: A crime against humanity, namely other inhumane acts, punishable under Article 5(i) read with Article 7(3) of the Statute of the Tribunal. "Statement of the facts. "The Republic of Croatia declared its independence on the 25th of June, 1991, by which time an armed conflict had erupted in some areas in Croatia between Croatian Serbs (Krajina Serbs) and Croatian forces. In September 1991, the Croatian Serbs and the Yugoslav People's Army (the "JNA") controlled about one-third of the territory of the Republic of Croatia. "On the 19th of December, 1991, the Assembly of the Serbian Autonomous Region of Krajina, together with the Serbs from other parts of the Republic of Croatia, declared independence from Croatia and purported to form a new entity, the self-proclaimed Republika Srpska Krajina (the "RSK"). The "RSK" had its own military force, the Serbian Army of Krajina or SVK. "The Krajina region comprising the former UNPA's Sector South and Sector North was situated within the "RSK" and included, but was not limited to, the municipalities of Benkovac, Donji Lapac, Drnis, Gospic, Gracac, Knin, Korenica, Obrovac, Sibenik, Sinj, and Zadar. "In February 1992, in accordance with the Vance Plan, the United Nations Security Council established under its authority a United Nations Protection Force, called UNPROFOR, that was to be deployed in the UNPA's in Croatian. The UNPA's were areas in Croatia where Serbs constituted the majority or a substantial minority of the population and where inter-communal tensions had already led to armed conflict. There were four UNPA's known as Sectors North, South, East, and West. "By 1992, the Croatian army was formulating plans for forcible re-taking of the territory of the "RSK." In 1992, 1993, 1994, and 1995, Croatian forces launched military operations with this ultimate objective. "These operations were launched into the UNPA's or adjacent "pink zones" in the Miljevacki Plateau in June 1992, the area of the Maslenica bridge in northern Dalmatia in January 1993, the Medak Pocket in September 1993, Operation Flash in Western Slovenia May 1995" --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Slavonija, not Slovenia.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Slavonija, excuse me. "In Western Slavonija in May 1995 and Operation Storm in August 1995. "Ivan Cermak was born on 19 December, 1949, in the municipality of Zagreb in the Republic of Croatia, then part of the SFRY. "Between 1990 and 1991, Ivan Cermak held the position of the vice-president of the Executive Board of the Croatian Democratic Union (HDZ) and also served as an advisor to President Franjo Tudjman. "In 1991, Ivan Cermak was appointed the Assistant Minister of Defence in the government of the Republic of Croatia, which position he held until 1993. Whilst in this position and thereafter he held the rank of colonel general. In 1993, he was appointed the Minister of Trade, Shipbuilding, and Energy. In December 1993, Ivan Cermak ceased to be a minister of the Croatian Gotovina. "On 5 August 1995, President Franjo Tudjman appointed Ivan Cermak the commander of the Knin Garrison. Ivan Cermak established his headquarters in Knin on 5 or 6 August 1995. "As the commander of the Knin Garrison, and pursuant to the authority conferred on him by President Franjo Tudjman, to who whom he was directly responsible, Ivan Cermak exercised de jure and/or de facto control over some of the Croatian forces operating in the southern portion of the Krajina region during Operation Storm from the time of his appointment and in the operation's aftermath. In particular, he exercised effective control over the units of the Special Police of the Ministry of the Interior of the Republic of Croatia (the "RH MUP"), and some elements of the HV including the Military Police and the civil administration, and through them, exercised territorial control over significant areas in which the crimes alleged in this Amended Indictment were committed. "On or about the 15th of November, 1995, Ivan Cermak was succeeded as the commander of Knin Garrison by his Deputy. "Mladen Markac was born on the 8th of May, 1955, in Djurdjevac, in the municipality of Djurdjevac in the Republic of Croatia, then part of the SFRY. "In 1981, Mladen Markac graduated from the University of Zagreb, and in 1982 he completed his compulsory military service. He then joined the police force of the Ministry of the Interior of the SFRY. "In 1990, Mladen Markac, and others, established a police unit for special tasks within the Ministry of the Interior. He was appointed Deputy Commander of the unit which, in late 1990, became the Anti-Terrorist Unit. In 1991 Mladen Markac was appointed the head of the Lucko Anti-Terrorist Unit. In 1992, he was promoted to the rank of Major General (reserve). "On 18 February 1994 Mladen Markac was appointed Commander of the RH MUP. In the aftermath of Operation Storm, Mladen Markac held the rank of Colonel General. "As commander of the Special Police of the RH MUP, during and after Operation Storm, Mladen Markac deployed and issued orders to the Special Police forces and otherwise exercised control over them."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thank you, Madam Registrar. I will relieve you when it comes to the schedule. And I want to make sure that I am right in this. Attached to the indictment there is only one schedule, Mr. Whiting. Is that correct? Initially in the original indictment there were two and what we have now with the amended indictment is one schedule referring to Counts 2 and 3, and it is a revised list of victims, and we don't have what was the other schedule relating to Counts 4 and 5.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: That's correct, Your Honour. And while I'm on my feet, if I could just make one clarification to Your Honour's very helpful procedural summary of the original indictment and this amended indictment, just to be clear, the original indictment was in fact unsealed and made public on July 26th, 2001. So the -- there has, in fact, been a public indictment against this accused for over four years.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Right. Thank you for pointing that out. I will deal myself with the schedule to this amended indictment. And the reason why I'm going into the details is this is a special Tribunal that attaches great importance to the role that victims play in these proceedings. This Tribunal also has a mandate from the Security Council of the United Nations to strive towards a reconciliation on the ground in the territories of the former Yugoslavia. And so we consider it important that the families of these alleged victims are aware that they have not been forgotten by this Tribunal. This is a schedule to the amended indictment, referring to Counts 2 and 3, and it deals with several villages and hamlets. I will go through the list very quickly. It gives the municipality, hamlet, or village; the date when the killing took place; the victim's name; the sex or gender - I prefer to use that word; the age, when it is available; and the manner of death. I'll start with the Benkovac municipality.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: So, Mr. Gotovina, please stand up.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: You have the following options today: You may opt -- as I ask you whether you wish to enter a plea, you may opt to plead guilty or not guilty to the seven counts that were read out today; you also have the right, if you want to, if you so choose, to delay pleading. In that case, pleading has to come forward or I can delay it only up to 30 days from today. You also have a right to remain completely silent. And if you remain completely silent, in 30 days' time from today, if you still remain silent, then I will enter a plea of not guilty on your behalf to each of the seven counts that were read out. I wish to know whether you have had an opportunity to discuss this with your duty counsel and whether you prepared to enter a plea today or whether you wish to delay or you wish to remain silent.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I have discussed this with my counsel, and I am prepared to plead today.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. I thank you. The first count that you are charged with, and you heard Madam Registrar reading it together with the other counts, is a charge of persecutions, a crime against humanity, which under the Statute of this Tribunal is punishable under Article 5(h). You were charged with persecutions, both with individual criminal responsibility, pursuant to Article 7(1) of the Statute, as well as under superior command responsibility pursuant to Article 7(3) of the Statute. How do you plead to this first count of persecution, guilty or not guilty?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, not guilty.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thank you, Mr. Gotovina. The second count is a charge of murder, which is a violation of the laws or customs of war, which is punishable under Article 3 of the Statute of this Tribunal. As regards this second count of murder, you are charged with superior responsibility pursuant to Article 7(3) of the Statute. How do you plead to this second count of murder, being a violation of the laws or customs of war?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Not guilty, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thank you, Mr. Gotovina. The third count is a charge of plunder of public or private property as being a violation of the laws or customs of war, also punishable under Article 3(e) of the Statute of this Tribunal. As far as this count is concerned, you're charged both under 7(1), that is individual criminal responsibility, and under 7(3), that is by way of superior command responsibility. How do you wish to plead to this third count, guilty or not guilty?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Not guilty, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thank you, Mr. Gotovina. The fourth count you're charged with is, as you've heard, a charge of wanton destruction of cities, towns, or villages, this being a violation of the laws or customs of war, also punishable under Article 3(b) of the Statute of this Tribunal. You are charged with regard to this fourth count, both under 7(1), Article 7(1), and Article 7(3) of our Statute, that is both under individual criminal responsibility and under superior command responsibility. How do you plead to this fourth count against you?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, not guilty.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. I thank you, Mr. Gotovina. The fifth count relates to a charge of deportation, this being a crime against humanity, which is punishable under Article 5(d) of the Statute of this Tribunal. Even here with regard to this fifth count, charge of deportation, you are charged both under Article 7(1) and Article 7(3) of the Statute, that is by way of individual criminal responsibility as well as by way of superior responsibility. How do you wish to plead to this fifth count against you, namely, one, deportation, a crime against humanity?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, not guilty.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you. The sixth charge is other inhumane acts, consisting of forced displacement, this being also a crime against humanity, punishable under Article 5(1)(i) of the Statute of this Tribunal. You are charged with this crime, both with individual criminal responsibility, pursuant to Article 7(1) of the Statute of this Tribunal, as well as under Article 7(3), that is with superior command responsibility. How do you wish to plead to this sixth count, other inhumane acts, being a crime against humanity, guilty or not guilty?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, not guilty.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you. The seventh and final count is a charge of other inhumane acts, a crime against humanity, punishable also under Article 5(i) of the Statute. You're charged with superior responsibility in this context pursuant to Article 7(3) of the Statute. How do you wish to plead to this seventh and final count, guilty or not guilty?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, not guilty.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. You may sit down. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Madam Registrar, I wish you to enter into the records of this case and note to the effect that the accused, upon being asked by the Presiding Judge, has entered a plea of not guilty to each and every one of the seven counts brought against him by the amended indictment.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Mr. Gotovina, it is also my duty pursuant to Rule 62 bis of the -- of our Rules of Procedure and Evidence that should you so wish at any later point in time, you can change your plea from one of not guilty to one of guilty in relation to either the entirety of the indictment or to one or more of the counts that were read out to you. Having said all, now I will quickly bring this Initial Appearance to an end by pointing out the following. I will now proceed to appoint a Pre-Trial Judge for your case. And the Pre-Trial Judge, which could be myself, will schedule a Status Conference to be held within the next 120 days from today. This will be pursuant to Rule 65 bis (a) of the Rules of Procedure and Evidence of this Tribunal. The purpose of such Status Conference is two-fold. First of all, it will give the Pre-Trial Judge, and also the pre-trial Chamber an opportunity to organise exchanges between the parties, Prosecution and Defence, and to facilitate, put in motion, the -- an expeditious preparation for trial. Secondly, the Pre-Trial Judge will have an opportunity to see you in person and make sure that your rights are being fully respected, that you are being treated well by the -- by our personnel at the Detention Unit as well as by your counsel and to be made aware of any complaints and requests that you may have. Later on you will be informed of the exact date of the Status Conference in due course, but as a newcomer to this Tribunal, may I point out that we take pride in having a Detention Unit which is model insofar as respect of detainees' rights are concerned. And you will have an opportunity to see for yourself and to assess for yourself the precision with which I am addressing this matter. I will also be giving instructions to the Registrar, Mr. Holthuis, to fix a date for trial when this becomes appropriate. Of course, between now and when a fixed date is fixed, is established, there will be the pre-trial process in place. And much depends on how quickly the pre-trial stage will proceed. In the meantime, until there is an order to the contrary, you will remain in custody pursuant to an order that I signed earlier on this morning. But as I explained to you earlier on, Rule 65 does entitle you to file a motion for provisional release. I'm sure that counsel that will be assigned to you will help you in this matter. I also wish to draw your attention to another rule that we have that is rarely referred to in initial appearances, and that is that there is nothing stopping the Prosecutor from seeking to question you, even at this stage, after your arraignment before this -- before me today. Rule 63 governs this matter, and I'm going to read it out to you so that you will be privy to the rights that you have should you be approached by a member from the Office of the Prosecutor, seeking an interview with you. The first paragraph of Rule 63 lays down that: "Questioning by the Prosecutor of an accused, including after the initial appearance," that is including even after today, "shall not proceed without the presence of counsel unless the accused has voluntarily and expressly agreed to proceed without counsel present. If the accused subsequently expresses a desire to have counsel, questioning shall thereupon cease and shall only resume when the accused's counsel is present." This is paragraph (B) now. "The questioning of any waiver to the right of counsel shall be audio-recorded or video-recorded in accordance with the procedure provided for in another Rule," that's Rule 43, "and the Prosecutor shall, at the beginning of the questioning, caution the accused in accordance with Rule 42(A)(iii)." Basically I will be brief here. The Prosecutor or the officer from the Office of the Prosecutor will be bound to caution you first and foremost as to your right to remain silent and that any statement that you may decide to make will be recorded and may be used in evidence. I would suggest that you ask the officer in charge at the Detention Unit to ask the Registrar to make available to you a copy of the Rules of Procedure and Evidence as well as of the Statute in your own language. They exist, they are available, and I think they would help you understand better a bit of our procedural rules. I also wish to avail myself of this Initial Appearance to remind you, Mr. Whiting, for and on behalf of the Prosecutor that pursuant to Rule 66(A)(i) of our Rules, you need to make available to Defence counsel in a language which the accused understands all the supporting material which accompanied the indictment when confirmation was sought. And this needs to be done within 30 days of the Initial Appearance, that is of today. I do appreciate, of course, that today we only have duty counsel and that we, strictly speaking, do not have proper Defence counsel yet assigned. But I think that would be something that should materialise in the next few days. Mr. Gotovina, also related to what I have just mentioned to the Prosecutor, you and your Defence counsel, in accordance with our Rule 72(A), you will have then a 30-day period for filing any preliminary motions that once you would have received all the supporting material in accordance with Rule 66 that I mentioned a minute ago, I entrust that matters are already underway to start discussions with you regarding the assignment of Defence counsel for the purpose of the pre-trial stage. And I am sure that your Defence counsel will take this matter up. If, in the meantime, until you are assigned a proper Defence counsel you need some legal advice, I can refer you to the commandant of the Detention Unit or directly to the registrar or his deputy. I can assure you they -- you will find them very forthcoming, and they will assist you with any request that you might have. Before I bring this Initial Appearance to an end, is there anything, Mr. Whiting, that you would like to raise at this stage on behalf of the Prosecution?

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: No, Your Honour, except to say that the OTP is well aware of its disclosure obligations and will seek to disclose the supporting materials promptly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. I thank you so much. And needless to say, this needs to be -- the Rule 66 disclosure needs to be in a language that the accused understands. Now, Mr. Gotovina, you will soon leave this courtroom. You've been here only a few days. I wish to know whether -- from you whether you wish to raise any matter. I also wish to know whether in these days following your arrest and surrender and transfer to The Hague, whether you have been treated well, and if you any matter that you would like me to -- like to address to me, please go ahead.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, no, I do not have anything to raise. Everything is fine. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. Thank you. Thank you. You may sit down. There being no other business to transact, no other matters to address, I declare this Initial Appearance ended here. Thank you.

procedural_notes.text: [Please refer to the Schedule to the Indictment]
